title: Finite-triple range comparisons transfer the Mittag–Leffler condition
statement: Let $T$ and $U$ be functors from a cofiltered category $J$ to possibly different universes of sets. Assume that for every pair of composable arrows $t\xrightarrow{g}m\xrightarrow{f}n$ there are bijections $e_n:T_n\to U_n$, $e_m:T_m\to U_m$ and $e_t:T_t\to U_t$ such that $e_nT(f)=U(f)e_m$ and $e_nT(gf)=U(gf)e_t$. The bijections may depend on the pair, and no relation between choices for different pairs is imposed. If $U$ is Mittag–Leffler [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system], then $T$ is Mittag–Leffler.

proof.text: Use the eventual-image criterion in [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system]. At n choose an arrow f:m→n whose U-image is contained in the image of every composite g≫f. For a given g choose its three bijections. Map an element of im T(f) by e_n, use the first commutative equation to place it in im U(f), and use stabilization to lift it through U(g≫f). Lift this preimage along the surjective e_t. The second commutative equation and injectivity of e_n show that the resulting T-element maps to the original one. Thus im T(f) is contained in im T(g≫f) for every g.
